articles.title: v8.0.0-rc.20-dev.1: chore(release): bump to 8.0.0-rc.20 (#30838)
articles.summary: Version 8.0.0-rc.19 → 8.0.0-rc.20 . Merging this PR publishes the release. The main change: the ORM's commands run on @prisma/cli-engine 0.9.0, the engine the prisma CLI 8.0.0-rc.25 ships ( #30835 ). A piped ORM command now prints tab-separated data lines on stdout; scripts that read JSON must pass --json . This release lets prisma/composer and prisma/prisma-cli drop their engine 0.7.0 pins. What to review Release notes: docs/releases/v8.0.0-rc.20.md , which becomes the GitHub Release body. It covers 11 merged PRs: 7 breaking changes, 7 features, 3 fixes. A type alias in PSL can set @default , @onCreate and @onUpdate , and the contract stores each column's real type instead of the alias name. Postgres migrations can rename, move and remove namespaces, and can change a relation's actions or a primary key. A failed migration check now names the object it expected. articles.title: openclaw 2026.10.6
articles.summary: 2026.10.6 Highlights Patched Node runtime required: OpenClaw now requires Node 24.22.1+ on the 24 line or 26.12.1+ on the 26 line, which reject TLS chains signed with the compromised certificate keys addressed in the October 2026 Node.js security releases. Docker images ship Node 24.22.1, installers select the patched runtimes, and openclaw update refuses with recovery guidance before installing on an older Node instead of breaking the running install. Source builds now pin pnpm 12.15.0. ( #179992 ) Thanks @joshavant . Safer updates and recovery: package swaps now refuse unsafe service...

articles.title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
articles.summary: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation News today from Anthropic: We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral. Today, we are donating the standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, which we co-founded with Block and OpenAI last year, and to which we donated the Model Context Protocol (MCP). I'm pleased to note I called this one last December , when Anthropic first declared skills to be an "open standard": I wouldn't be surprised to see this end up in the AAIF , recently the new home of the MCP specification....
